title: The Defense of Skylight Refuge
dek: Hunters close on the people beneath the canyon. A diversion draws some away while three defenders hold the approach. Saving the Refuge takes desperate magic, an immediate revival and a renewed battle that ends with Nymera’s ashes.

facts.Setting: Skylight Refuge and its wooded, stepped approach
facts.People: Eugene; Arjahn; Nymera; Olokun; Elenia; Scribonia; the Refuge civilians
facts.Outcome: The Refuge and civilians survive. Nymera is revived after her first death, then reduced to ash in the renewed attack.

body:
Hunters close on the people beneath the canyon. A diversion draws some away while three defenders hold the approach. Saving the Refuge takes desperate magic, an immediate revival and a renewed battle that ends with Nymera’s ashes.

The hideout is being found

The canyon delayed the morning sun, but it could not silence the jungle. Hunters were moving above the Refuge, listening and smelling for the people below. The company could no longer rely on concealment alone. Arjahn looked at a shelter that had been reinforced only a little and feared it could become a coffin.

Olokun proposed drawing the hunters away. Scribonia wanted additional wards, but they did not mistake those for a defense against everything outside. Arjahn would stay with the civilians in case the diversion failed. Eugene immediately refused to let him defend alone. Nymera, newer to the terrain, agreed to remain too.

The split became clear: Olokun, Elenia and Scribonia would move along known paths and try to pull the danger toward the river. Arjahn, Eugene and Nymera would protect the people left behind. Eugene gave Arjahn a diamond before they separated. Nymera asked the others to come back.

Ground away from the civilians

Arjahn searched for an emergency route or a place to seal the refugees behind stone. Neither option was a simple rescue: a sealed chamber needed air, and an opened passage might send unprotected people into the jungle. Fighting where they slept risked bringing the attack onto them.

Eugene remembered a place a little away from the camp with open sky and a clear line of sight toward the cliffs. His long habit of finding somewhere to read unexpectedly became useful knowledge. The defenders moved there so that the first attack would find them rather than the civilians.

Arjahn assigned Nymera the enemies that came close, relied on Eugene’s striking power and promised to keep both fighting as long as he could. Nymera tried to use height and cover; Eugene stayed farther back. Some hunters had followed the diversion. Others had not been fooled, or preferred the easier prey still below.

Holding spends the defenders

The first attackers struck Nymera while Eugene answered from range. Arjahn tried to conserve what he might need later, then was knocked down and burned by binding webbing. The fight was already taking more from them than a cautious plan had allowed.

A larger horror appeared with a mouth as wide as a house. Arjahn told Nymera that, if he had to choose between her and the refugees, the refugees would come first. She asked for more than that: they were in this together, and she needed help to move. He said the words of a soldier prepared to die, while wondering what the island was making of him.

Nymera held. Eugene abandoned some of his restraint and sent lightning through the attackers. Arjahn poured healing into wounds that kept opening. They bought a short breathing space, not a victory that would let them rest. Something else was already coming through the trees.

The Wish and the first return

Another creature came from the earth with a burning, malevolent eye. Nymera was swallowed while Eugene struggled to stop the defenders from being overwhelmed. Arjahn sent Scribonia a message that sounded like farewell: they were outside the shelter, depleted, losing, and still trying to protect the refugees. Only static answered.

Eugene used Wish. The two attackers burst apart in a terrible rain of blood and debris. Nymera’s dead body fell with their remains. The magic had ended the immediate threat; it had not brought every defender through it alive.

Arjahn flew to her and cast Revivify. Nymera returned, and the diamond was not consumed on this return. He held her, sobbing, and for a moment called her by his daughter’s name before correcting himself. They were not the same person. His grief had broken through the hard assurance he had offered earlier. He apologized for saying he could leave her to die.

Nymera thought she had fallen asleep. She rose and hugged him. Eugene could barely remain standing after what he had spent. The three helped one another back toward the Refuge, with Nymera already thinking about food for the companions who had gone away.

The diversion comes home

The defenders could hear distant power in the jungle without knowing all that was happening to their friends. Eugene brought attention back to what they could still do: make sure the refugees were safe. Arjahn washed blood from their bodies. They waited.

Then Scribonia returned in a flash with Olokun and Elenia. Elenia was bleeding badly. Scribonia’s body was cracked and burned, one arm scarcely held together. Olokun warned that something was preventing Elenia’s wounds from closing. The distraction had brought the company back alive and in urgent need of care.

It had also brought a trail. The hunters could follow so much fresh blood. Arjahn and Nymera gave what healing they could while Scribonia worked against the curse. Elenia in turn repaired Scribonia’s injuries. Cleaning away blood might help, but the trees were already shaking. Two wounded beasts were coming to finish them.

The second loss

Arjahn withdrew, too exhausted to be useful in another fight. Nymera stayed despite her wounds. Eugene would not run while the civilians remained in danger. Olokun and Scribonia met the returning monsters with the strength they had left, while Elenia continued giving help and attacks as she moved back.

One beast breathed decay over Elenia. The other burrowed into position and turned its burning eye on Nymera. This time she became ash. There was no body for another immediate Revivify. Olokun saw the woman who had cared for his sister disappear and pressed his attack harder.

Scribonia removed one attacker from the field, giving the others room to deal with the great reptilian beast. Eugene kept drawing on himself to cast. His final strike brought it down. When the remaining creature returned, Scribonia destroyed it with a ray, leaving dust where another source of danger had stood.

The jungle fell quiet. The Refuge was safe. Nymera was still lost. Those facts belonged to the same victory.

Ashes carried forward

Eugene asked whether anything could be done for Nymera. Elenia told him to bring her violet ashes. He gathered them, hoping it would be enough. The survivors went back to the shelter; Arjahn was found asleep at its entrance with his claws still extended.

The record continues later. Before the mountain offensive, Eugene hands Elenia the ashes. Afterward she calls Nymera back over them. A later living appearance shows that Nymera’s story did continue, but it does not identify the exact second restoration spell or turn the ash recovery into the earlier Revivify.

The defense had preserved people and a foothold. It had also exhausted the company and made the idea of waiting for the next attack harder to bear. The next offensive would grow from those pressures, with no agreement that everyone wanted the same thing from destroying the enemy’s mountain.
